articles.title: ‘I had a better life in Iran’: Afghan women forced home struggle to rebuild
articles.summary: For five years, Zahra cared for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by. Now back in Herat, western Afghanistan, the 28-year-old trained midwife is unemployed. She lives with her parents and siblings, apart from her six-year-old son, who lives with her ex-husband.

articles.title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
articles.summary: When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic. Both were later looted and destroyed.

articles.title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.

articles.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
articles.summary: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can…

articles.title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
articles.summary: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
articles.summary: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.
